latest_census.notes: Population and Housing Census of Malaysia 2020 (MyCensus 2020), enumeration ended 31 October 2021; 32.4 million (29.8m citizens). Ethnicity: Bumiputera 69.4% / Chinese 23.1% / Indians 6.7% / others 0.8% of citizens. Religion: 2020 census gives Muslim 63.5%, Buddhist ~19%, Christian 9%, Hindu 6.1%. Language: the census portal says the questionnaire ran to over 100 questions, but no result confirmed a mother-tongue/language question; left null.

tier_reason: Ethnicity from the 2020 census round is machine-readable (Parquet/API, CC BY 4.0) on OpenDOSM by administrative district (160 vs 159 admin2 shapes) and by state (16 = admin1). Religion is asked but no subnational religion table surfaced this session.
recommended_action: Read OpenDOSM population_district and population_state (2020 rows) for ethnicity at admin2 and admin1; confirm in the technical notes (open.dosm.gov.my/publications/technical-notes/population-technotes) whether 2020 is the census count. Then search DOSM for religion by state/district from Census 2020 (Banci 2020 'agama' tables) and check the Key Findings: Administrative District publication for a religion table. Establish whether the census asked language before declaring it.

summary: Malaysia's 2020 census asked ethnicity and religion. OpenDOSM publishes ethnicity (Malay, other Bumiputera, Chinese, Indian, other citizen, non-citizen) by administrative district and by state as Parquet/API under CC BY 4.0, with district counts (160) matching the map's 159 admin2 shapes almost exactly and 16 states matching admin1 -- build ethnicity next. Subnational religion and any language question remain to be established; the DOSM 'Key Findings: Administrative District' release is the place to look for religion by district.
